title: Bliss Street — AUB frontage
note: Architectural reconstruction from published AUB photographs and mapped footprints. Approximate dimensions, no invented landmark identities. Terrain elevation sampled directly from the current city mesh.

sources.use: Footprint corners and orientation
Official coordinate cross-check: 33°53′58.19″N,35°28′56.23″E
Symmetric gatehouse, horseshoe arch, paired towers and terracotta pitched roofs; visual reference only, not used as texture
Sandstone, yellow trim and wrought iron
Southern campus boundary trace
Campus wall edge along Bliss Street
Ashlar campus wall, pale coping and estimated height; image is a modelling reference, not a new texture
Named AssemblyHall footprint; nave, transept and apse
AUB identifies AssemblyHall as formerchapel with redroof tiles and rosewindows
Stonewalls, pointedgables, windows, buttresses, redtiled crossingroofs
Named DaoukMosque footprint
Lowarched streetarcade, flatroof, slendercylindrical minaret with gallery andsmallpointedlantern
Mapped Cuban-laurel trunk coordinate, evergreen broadleaved tree; canopy dimensions are estimated

Highly oblique view points west down street, with facade normal cosine only 0.224. The right-hand building is visible but the photo cannot reliably distinguish the exact target frontage from nearer sections.
The target is behind a high campus boundary wall and dense trees. No target building facade or floor count is visible.
A two-level campus facade is visible behind the smooth block boundary. Roof/eave and two windows on each visible level are clear, but trees conceal the right half and boundary hides lower portion.

Pale campus masonry facade is visible above tall stone boundary, but top and base are cropped and tree branches cover side openings. Three tall windows and part of a higher level are observable; full width/height unknown.
Large trees and a shaded stone wall conceal target. A small upper building/eave fragment at top right provides no reliable floor or opening count.
Long rough stone boundary and dense trees block the candidate. Small roof/building fragments cannot establish floors or bay rhythm.
A pale stone campus building is visible behind iron fence and trees. Only fragments of two levels are exposed; total floors and full bay count remain unknown.
Camera looks along the street. Target on the campus side is screened by trees/fence; the large white grid tower at right is the opposite-side neighboring building and must not be assigned to491.
Dense foliage fills virtually the entire image. No facade, window count, storey count or roof is observable for the target.
